title: Kaffara in Islam: How to Give Kaffara Fasting Expiation by Feeding the Poor
content:
What Is Kaffara in Islam?

At Daan Foundation, Amroha, we believe feeding the poor through zakat, sadqah, and iftaar is the best form of charity in Islam — and the same holds true for kaffara, one of the most misunderstood obligations of Ramadan. If you have missed fasts without a valid reason, kaffara in islam is the expiation Allah has prescribed to make up for that lapse.

Kaffara in islam simply means feeding sixty poor people for each fast you missed intentionally. It is not a fine the state collects, and it is not something you can pray away — it is a practical act of charity that turns a mistake into food on the table of a struggling family. It also sits naturally alongside other Ramadan obligations — zakat, sadqah, and iftar charity — which is why donors often complete them together in one giving season. Kaffara fasting rules apply when a fast is broken deliberately without a shariah-approved excuse, and the redemption is paid through kaffara feeding for poor families.

Kaffara in Islam: The Rules You Need to Know

Before you calculate how much to give, understand when kaffara actually applies. Islamic scholars describe kaffara fasting expiation in these terms: it becomes due when a healthy adult breaks a Ramadan fast intentionally — through eating, drinking, or sexual intercourse — without a valid reason. This is different from qada, where you simply make up a missed fast on another day. Kaffara is heavier because it involves a penalty, and the Islamic ruling on kaffara is clear: feed sixty needy people per fast, or free a slave, or fast sixty consecutive days.

In practical terms, most donors in India fulfil kaffara through feeding, because it is the option that most directly matches the spirit of the act — nourishing the same community the fast was meant to serve. That is why kaffara donation india is usually routed through a food charity ngo rather than a general collection box.

Kaffara vs Fidyah: Never Confuse the Two

Many people ask us the difference between fidyah and kaffara, and the answer matters because the amounts and the reasons are different. Fidyah is paid by someone who permanently cannot fast — an elderly person or someone with a chronic illness — and the rate is roughly the cost of one meal per missed day. Kaffara, by contrast, is the penalty for a deliberately broken fast and carries the far heavier burden of feeding sixty people.

When donors mix the two, they either overpay or underpay their obligation, and in some cases they think they have cleared a kaffara fasting due when they have only covered fidyah — or the reverse. A reliable islamic donation platform should explain this difference clearly on its kaffara donation page, and should keep fidyah and kaffara collections separate so the money reaches the poor in the correct way and you can give both obligations their due weight.

How to Give Kaffara: Step by Step

If you owe kaffara, here is the simplest way to complete it with confidence, especially if you are giving from outside Amroha:

  1. Count exactly how many fasts were broken deliberately — the number drives everything else.
  2. Confirm the feeding rate per person at your chosen charity, so you know your donation feeds sixty people per fast.
  3. Give through a verified islamic charity ngo that publishes its food distribution reports.
  4. Prefer a dedicated kaffara feeding option rather than a general donation.
  5. Keep the payment confirmation for your records and for spiritual peace of mind.

At Daan Foundation, one full meal for the poor through our year-round Community Kitchen costs approximately ₹59 per person. So for one kaffara fast, a donation of sixty such meals — around ₹3,540 — feeds sixty people, and you can scale that figure by the number of fasts you owe.

How Daan Foundation Helps with Kaffara and Food for Poor

When you give kaffara through us, your donation becomes meals, not numbers. Our Amroha-based community kitchen cooks and distributes food daily to families who cannot afford regular meals, and during Ramzan our kitchen runs additional feeding drives. That is why donors across India trust us for kaffara donation india — the act ends in a plate of food, not a receipt in a drawer.

If you are ready to complete your kaffara fasting obligation, donate now and choose the kaffara feeding option so your gift is directed exactly where it belongs — to the poor who need it most, and in the exact spirit the expiation was designed for.

Where Daan Foundation Works

Our established base is Amroha, Uttar Pradesh, where the community kitchen and zakat donation in Amroha programs run all year. Beyond Amroha, we run time-bound pilot projects during Ramadan, with iftar stalls and feeding points set up in different parts of India based on need and local partnerships. Donors from Kerala, Bengaluru and Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, West Bengal, Jammu and Kashmir, Gujarat, and Hyderabad and Telangana regularly reach out to fulfil kaffara and fidyah through our network — and our pilot model lets their giving reach verified families wherever the need is real.

Kaffara FAQ

What is kaffara in islam and how is it paid?

Kaffara is the expiation for a deliberately broken Ramadan fast. It is paid by feeding sixty poor people per fast, and most people in India fulfil it through a food charity ngo that runs kaffara feeding for poor families.

How much kaffara cost for one fast?

Kaffara cost depends on the per-meal rate of the charity you choose. At Daan Foundation, one community kitchen meal costs ₹59 per person, so one kaffara fast works out to sixty meals — roughly ₹3,540 — feeding sixty people.

Can I give kaffara donation online?

Yes. A verified islamic charity ngo like Daan Foundation accepts kaffara donation online via UPI and bank transfer, and routes it specifically toward feeding the poor through its kitchen.

Kaffara ya fidyah — kaunsa kab dena chahiye?

Fidyah tab diya jata hai jab aap permanently fast nahi kar sakte, jaise budhape ya beemari mein. Kaffara tab diya jata hai jab aapne jaankar ek fast toda ho. Rate aur reason dono alag hain — dono ko milakar nahi dena chahiye.

Give Your Kaffara with Full Confidence

Completing kaffara is not a punishment — it is a door to generosity. By turning one lapse into sixty meals, you bring real relief to families who struggle to eat, and you fulfill your obligation in the way Islam intends. If you still have questions about your kaffara fasting due, write to us at daanfoundationindia@gmail.com or donate now, and our team will guide you through the right amount. Feed the poor this Ramadan, and let your kaffara become someone's iftar — that is charity in its truest form.
